review: Stanza 1 is a fourfold acclamation of the one love under three aspects; Hebrew uses the construct 'Your love is healing / sufficing / full' so the four short lines stay parallel.
1:1–1:3 אַהֲבָתְךָ as the opening of each line: the Arabic repeats بِحُبِّكَ, and the anaphora is what carries the tune.
2:3 בַּחֻלְשָׁה — 'in weakness' (the noun is post-biblical but liturgical); the Arabic الضَّعْف is the point of the paradox, so it is kept rather than paraphrased.
3:4 וּבִנְטִישָׁה בְּלִי רֵעַ — the Arabic splits 'and the forsaking' across the line break (وَالـ / ـتَّرْكِ); Hebrew cannot split the word, so line 4 carries the whole phrase.
4:4 עַל־רֹאשְׁךָ חָבִיב — the Arabic has 'over Your head, O Beloved'; Hebrew repeats עַל־רֹאשְׁךָ from 4:3 because a bare חָבִיב would lose the address.
